reason: The heart and vessels seem like the starting point for a returning blood circuit.
expectation: I expect them to form a circuit that carries blood, though I am unsure how the return route will be shown.

alternatives.reason: Breathing muscles and lungs should make the air-moving route, but I chose to build the blood circuit first.

effect: Circulation forms a returning route that can carry supplies to cells and take substances away; the air-moving route is still needed.
reaction: The pump-and-return explanation makes the circuit's purpose clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it addresses the goal of moving air.
expectation: I expect the breathing muscles to help the lungs move air, though I do not yet know how the game will explain that movement.

effect: The breathing muscles move air by changing chest volume, and the next goal is to connect the lungs to circulation.
reaction: The explanation of inhaling and quiet exhaling made the mechanics clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it connects breathing to blood flow.
expectation: I expect it to show how oxygen passes from the lungs into the blood, though I am unsure how much detail it will give.

effect: The result completes the route: oxygen enters the blood in the lungs, while carbon dioxide travels back to the lungs to be breathed out. It also clarifies that blood returns to the heart between the lungs and the body.
reaction: The complete route was satisfying, though I wanted a little more detail about where the gases cross.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the breathing lungs to circulation was most worthwhile because it brought air movement, blood flow and gas exchange together in one route.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making circulation was the least engaging action because the compatible menu made the pairing predictable, although the explanation of a returning circuit was useful.

surprise.text: The final result clarified that blood returns to the heart after passing through the lungs before being sent to the body.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary: each paired parts with a clear role in breathing or circulation. The menu supplied compatible pairs, so choosing them did not demonstrate that I had discovered their compatibility.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how oxygen is used by the arm. The explanations were clear, though the predictable choices offered limited challenge; completing them does not establish that students understood the biology.
